question: A vegetable vendor bought 100 kg of potatoes at the rate of Rs. 19 per kg and spent Rs. 100 as cartage. He sold 60 kg of potatoes with a 50% profit and half of the remaining stock with a 40% profit. He sold half of the still remaining potatoes with a 25% profit. What profit percentage should he aim for when selling the ultimate remaining potatoes to achieve an overall profit of 42%?
solution:
**Given:**

A vegetable vendor bought 100 kg of potatoes at the rate of Rs. 19 per kg and spent Rs. 100 as cartage. He sold 60 kg of potatoes with a 50% profit and half of the remaining stock with a 40% profit.

**Formula used:**

Total Cost Price (CP) = (Cost per kg × Total kg) + Cartage

Profit Percentage (PP) = dfrac{Selling Price (SP) - Cost Price (CP)}{Cost Price (CP)} times 100

**Calculations:**

Total CP = (19 × 100) + 100 = Rs. 2000

So, CP of 1 kg Potato = 2000 / 100 = Rs. 20
